summary.text: A 44-year-old African American man with long-standing treatment-resistant schizophrenia and a seizure disorder had been in sustained remission for 26 years on clozapine 300 mg/day (started 1998), living with his mother, who supervised adherence, attending a psychiatric day program and taking valproic acid for seizure prophylaxis.

On November 25, 2023 he presented to the emergency department with acute right leg swelling and pain; he was afebrile with oxygen saturation 99% on room air and had swelling, erythema, warmth, tenderness, firm induration and venous engorgement of the right thigh and calf, leukocytosis (WBC 12.6 × 10³/µL) and D-dimer >7,650 ng/mL. Blood cultures were obtained and empiric intravenous cefepime and vancomycin started. CT pulmonary angiography showed a right upper-lobe pulmonary embolism and venous Doppler ultrasound corroborated extensive deep vein thrombosis.

Clozapine was permanently discontinued (abrupt cessation, chosen collaboratively with the family) because of its known association with VTE; therapeutic enoxaparin was transitioned to apixaban 5 mg BID and he was discharged on December 12, 2023 on aripiprazole 5 mg daily.

Rapid relapse followed: thought blocking, suspiciousness, auditory hallucinations, safety-seeking behaviors and persecutory delusions. Aripiprazole was raised to 15 mg (by February 2024), 20 mg (April 2024) and 30 mg (by October 2024) with persisting persecutory delusions, command hallucinations, negative and cognitive symptoms and marked functional decline despite full adherence. Olanzapine 5 mg was added in March 2025 and titrated to 10 mg by April 2025 with suboptimal response.

On April 15, 2025 he was taken by EMS to a CPEP with acute psychotic exacerbation and behavioral disorganization and was admitted April 15-May 9, 2025: aripiprazole was tapered off, xanomeline–trospium started at 50/20 mg BID and titrated to 100/20 mg BID, olanzapine 5 mg morning/10 mg bedtime, valproic acid and apixaban continued, with bowel regimens; at discharge he denied active hallucinations with occasional self-directed speech and reduced verbal spontaneity.

Follow-up showed moderate improvement on May 20, 2025 with mild paranoid ideation; by June 3 renewed suspiciousness was followed by xanomeline–trospium 125/30 mg BID; on June 17 there was modest improvement and no recurrence of VTE; by July 14 significant stabilization with greater independence; on July 29 he was free of hallucinations and paranoid ideation; on August 26 telehealth showed no psychotic symptoms with only occasional, less frequent self-talk. Caregiver psychoeducation was provided. The authors report considerable improvement without significant adverse effects, as a single case.

Blood culture result, DVT site/side, and the nature of the pre-1998 antipsychotic trials are not reported.
